records.summary: Hohem's 2.5 kg camera gimbal with a tracking camera built in: it follows people, pets, vehicles and other subjects without a phone app, and its 1.4-inch touchscreen remote detaches to show the tracking camera's view from about 10 m away. On payload alone, Zhiyun's Weebill 3E ($199, 3 kg) and Feiyu's SCORP 3 ($299, 3.5 kg) carry more for less.
records.fit: Solo shooters filming themselves, a pet or a car with a mirrorless camera, who also want one gimbal for a phone and an action camera. Anyone who only needs steady footage from a camera under 2 kg can spend less on a DJI RS 3 Mini ($199) or RS 4 Mini ($309).
caveats: Digital Camera World's George Cairns, with a Sony A7 and 24mm f/1.4 lens (about 1.05 kg), saw occasional pan-motor twitches, and the camera flopped over in POV roll mode despite being well under the 2.5 kg rating.

Fstoppers' Zhen Siang Yang found the remote's live view frames differently from the camera, most of all beyond 35mm, with no way to calibrate it; ProVideo Coalition's Iain Anderson says it shows only roughly what is in shot.
Fstoppers also notes the battery cannot be swapped, the axis locks are manual, and there is no weather sealing.
Camera Jabber's Ali Jennings rates the finish and grip comfort a step below DJI and Zhiyun at this price.

Maker-stated limits: the gimbal must be rebalanced after switching between horizontal and vertical, the 20-hour figure is with tracking off and the gimbal still, and the Spot Mini focus motor and twist handle come only with the $384.99 Pro Kit. At 1,070 g it is 180 g heavier than the DJI RS 4 Mini (890 g).
records.question_served: Camera gimbal with built-in AI tracking that follows pets, vehicles and objects as well as people, works without the phone app, and lets a solo shooter check framing on a detachable remote, for about $315. It does not win on payload per dollar or on weight.

records.summary: Hohem's 765 g camera gimbal with a people-tracking camera and a fill light built in, for $198.99. It is lighter than Feiyu's SCORP Mini 3 Kit (940 g) and is rated for 17 hours against the Feiyu's 14, but the Feiyu costs $189 and carries 2 kg where the MT3 is rated for 1.4 kg.
records.fit: People who film themselves with a phone, a compact camera or a small mirrorless camera with a kit lens and want the lightest tracking gimbal they can carry all day. For a full-frame body with a standard zoom, the Feiyu SCORP Mini 3 Kit ($189), DJI RS 3 Mini ($199) or Hohem's own MT3 Pro is the better buy.
caveats: Digital Camera World's Paul Hatton calls the 1.4 kg rating unrealistic: a Canon 6D with a 24-105mm lens rolled forward, and the 770 g body alone was only just held steady.
Hatton also found the tracking sometimes slow to lock onto a face; it follows people only, not pets or objects.
Fstoppers' Zhen Siang Yang saw erratic behavior with a very light load (an Osmo 360), and notes just four motor-strength steps and a fixed 0.4-inch screen.
CGMagazine's Joe Findlay got 12 to 13 hours with everything running, not the 17 hours Hohem quotes for a still gimbal with tracking off.
Maker-stated limits: the gimbal must be rebalanced after switching between horizontal and vertical, and there is no detachable remote or focus motor option.
records.question_served: Lightest camera gimbal with a built-in AI tracker (no phone app) for a phone or a small mirrorless camera, at about $200: 765 g against 940 g for the Feiyu SCORP Mini 3 Kit and 1,000 g for the SCORP Mini 3 Pro. Marginal win: it loses on payload (1.4 kg against 2 kg) and costs $10 more than the Feiyu kit.

left_out.product: Hohem iSteady MT2 Kit ($199.90; without AI sensor $169)
left_out.why: Superseded at the same price by the MT3 ($198.99): 1.2 kg payload against 1.4 kg, clip-on tracker against built-in, older motors (Hohem says MT3 torque is 20% higher). Its one edge is weight (653 g against 765 g). At $169 without the tracker it loses to the Feiyu SCORP Mini 3 Kit ($189, 2 kg, tracking built in) and DJI RS 3 Mini ($199, 2 kg).

The store page does not list the kit's contents in text (an image file name suggests the HPL-R01 light and briefcase handle), so no named use could be verified. The extra $123 over the M7 already listed is for accessories, which the program pays nothing on.
Same gimbal plus focus motor, twist handle and case for $70 more; Fstoppers found the Spot Mini Motor can slip. The plain MT3 Pro is the record; the Kit is a variant on the same page.

notes: All Hohem prices and availability read live from store.hohem.com product .js on 2026-11-18; they match the saved catalog.

MT3 Pro is the clear pick. MT3 is a marginal second: it wins only on weight and rated battery life among tracking gimbals near $200, and Digital Camera World says its payload rating is optimistic. Drop it if only clear wins should be listed.
MT3 payload conflict on Hohem's own pages: hohem.com and the store comparison table say 1.4 kg; the store's separate MT3 page says 1.2 kg. The record uses 1.4 kg.
MT3 box conflict: the store's option text does not name a phone clamp or action camera adapter; CGMagazine and Fstoppers say a phone holder is included. Could not verify from Hohem's store.

Returns conflict: the refund policy says 7 days and that sale items cannot be canceled or refunded; the MT3 Pro page FAQ mentions 30-day returns and the page shows a 30-day price match badge. The record follows the policy page.
MT2 promotion: the store already shows the MT2 Kit at $199.90 against $369 (46% off). Could not verify whether the network's '20% off MT2 Kit' is a code that stacks on top; that needs a cart test.
